llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了SLM制备CoCrMo合金的时效行为，未涉及多孔结构、应力屏蔽或骨整合等核心方向。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of aging heat treatment on the microstructure and mechanical properties of CoCrMo alloys fabricated by selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Aging treatments at various temperatures and durations were applied to SLM-fabricated CoCrMo samples, followed by microstructural characterization and mechanical testing.
summary_en.result: Aging significantly altered the microstructure, leading to changes in hardness and tensile properties, with optimized aging conditions improving overall performance.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through optical and electron microscopy, hardness measurements, and tensile tests.

papers.title: Selective laser melting of Zn–Ag alloys for bone repair: microstructure, mechanical properties and degradation behaviour
papers.abstract: Zn possesses good biodegradability and biocompatibility, but its strength and hardness are insufficient for bone implants. In this study, Ag was introduced into Zn to improve the mechanical properties by selective laser melting. The results showed that Ag was dissolved in Zn, which generated constitutional undercooling in front of the advancing solid/liquid interface during solidification, making more nucleation events occur and thus refining the grains. When Ag content exceeded its solid solubility in Zn, AgZn3 phase is formed, which acted as active nucleation sites for Zn grains, further refining the grains. The refinement of the grains effectively hindered the plastic deformation and dislocation. As a result, the compressive strength and hardness were improved by about 100% and 116%, respectively. When Ag content continued increasing and became excessive, AgZn3 phase grew rapidly, coarsening the grains. Accordingly, the mechanical properties slightly decreased. These results demonstrated that the Zn–Ag alloys are potential implant biomaterials.

summary_en.motivation: Zinc's insufficient mechanical properties for bone implants motivated alloying with silver via selective laser melting to improve strength and hardness.
summary_en.method: Zn-Ag alloys with varying Ag content were fabricated by selective laser melting, and microstructure evolution was characterized.
summary_en.result: Addition of Ag refined grains via constitutional undercooling and AgZn3 nucleation, enhancing compressive strength and hardness by approximately 100% and 116%, respectively.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical properties were validated through uniaxial compression tests and hardness measurements.

papers.title: On the role of heat and mass transfer into laser processability during selective laser melting AlSi12 alloy based on a randomly packed powder-bed
papers.abstract: A newly transient mesoscopic model with a randomly packed powder-bed has been proposed to investigate the heat and mass transfer and laser process quality between neighboring tracks during selective laser melting (SLM) AlSi12 alloy by finite volume method (FVM), considering the solid/liquid phase transition, variable temperature-dependent properties and interfacial force. The results apparently revealed that both the operating temperature and resultant cooling rate were obviously elevated by increasing the laser power. Accordingly, the resultant viscosity of liquid significantly reduced under a large laser power and was characterized with a large velocity, which was prone to result in a more intensive convection within pool. In this case, the sufficient heat and mass transfer occurred at the interface between the previously fabricated tracks and currently building track, revealing a strongly sufficient spreading between the neighboring tracks and a resultant high-quality surface without obvious porosity. By contrast, the surface quality of SLM-processed components with a relatively low laser power notably weakened due to the limited and insufficient heat and mass transfer at the interface of neighboring tracks. Furthermore, the experimental surface morphologies of the top surface were correspondingly acquired and were in full accordance to the calculated results via simulation.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the role of heat and mass transfer between neighboring tracks on the laser processability of AlSi12 alloy during selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: A transient mesoscopic model with a randomly packed powder-bed was developed using the finite volume method, incorporating solid/liquid phase transition and temperature-dependent properties.
summary_en.result: Higher laser power elevated operating temperature and cooling rate, reducing viscosity and enhancing convection, leading to improved surface quality without porosity.
summary_en.validation: Experimental surface morphologies of the top surface were acquired and showed full agreement with the simulation results.

papers.title: [Application of plasma sprayed zirconia coating in dental implant: study in implant].
papers.abstract: Objective: To investigate the osseointegration of a novel coating-plasma-sprayed zirconia in dental implant. Methods: Zirconia coating on non-thread titanium implant was prepared using plasma spraying, the implant surface morphology, surface roughness and wettability were measured. In vivo, zirconia coated implants were inserted in rabbit tibia and animals were respectively sacrificed at 2, 4, 8 and 12 weeks after implantation. The bond strength between implant and bone was measured by push-out test. The osseointegration was observed by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), micro CT and histological analyses. Quantified parameters including removal torque, and bone-implant contact (BIC) percentage were calculated. Results: The surface roughness (1.6 µm) and wettability (54.6°) of zirconia coated implant was more suitable than those of titanium implant (0.6 µm and 74.4°) for osseointegration. At 12 weeks, the push-out value of zirconia coated implant and titanium implant were (64.9±3.0) and (50.4±2.9) N, and BIC value of these two groups were (54.7±3.6)% and (41.5±3.6)%. All these differences had statistical significance. Conclusions: The surface characters of zirconia coated implant were more suitable for osseointegration and present better osseointegration than smooth titanium implant in vivo, especially at early stage.

summary_zh.method: 在钛种植体上制备氧化锆涂层，植入兔胫骨并进行组织学与力学测试
summary_zh.result: 氧化锆涂层表面粗糙度和润湿性更优，12周时推出力和BIC均显著高于钛种植体

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate whether plasma-sprayed zirconia coating improves osseointegration of dental implants compared to smooth titanium.
summary_en.method: Zirconia coating was applied on non-threaded titanium implants via plasma spraying, and implants were inserted into rabbit tibiae for up to 12 weeks.
summary_en.result: Zirconia-coated implants showed higher surface roughness and wettability, and significantly higher push-out force and bone-implant contact at 12 weeks.
summary_en.validation: In vivo animal study with histological, micro-CT, and mechanical push-out tests at multiple time points.
